h1: Mira Montra Resort Koh Mak — Quiet Beachfront Villas on Ao Phra That Many Rate the Best on Koh Mak
intro: Koh Mak is the island people come to for quiet, not for parties — and Mira Montra Resort Koh Mak understands that perfectly · A 4-star boutique resort on Ao Phra Beach on the island's north side, made up of beachfront villas and sea-view rooms climbing a small hill · There's an outdoor pool looking out to the sea, a genuinely quiet private beach, and free kayaks and SUP boards · The draws are the calm atmosphere, the attentive service, and food many guests rave about · From approx. ฿2,500/night, scoring 9.0 from around 66 reviews

The open-air beachfront restaurant at Mira Montra Resort Koh Mak

body.html: Mira Montra sits on Ao Phra Beach on the north side of Koh Mak, the small, famously quiet island sitting between Koh Chang and Koh Kood · The resort splits into two parts — villas right by the sand, and a cluster of sea-view rooms climbing the hill behind them · The first thing guests mention is the atmosphere: the private beach in front is genuinely quiet, with no shops or loud music nearby, exactly right for people who came to truly switch off.

There's a good range of rooms — the Hilltop Sea View Room is the cheapest entry option, then Deluxe Villa and Beachfront Deluxe Villa (one-bedroom villas), up to the two-bedroom Family Villa · Villas add bathtubs, outdoor showers and, on some, rooftop decks · Every room has comfy beds, a mini fridge, complimentary water and snacks, a balcony and a good-pressure shower · A point guests consistently praise is how clean both the rooms and the shared spaces are.

"Staff picked us up from the boat, free kayaks and SUP, complimentary afternoon tea, the private beach was so quiet and the pool looks out over the sea — the best-cared-for, best-atmosphere resort we've stayed at on Koh Mak."

The stars here are the outdoor pool looking out to the sea and the quiet, clean private beach · There are plenty of sun loungers around the pool · The resort lends out kayaks and SUP boards for free — a favourite with guests — while snorkelling trips and motorbike rentals cost extra · The restaurant is open-air by the beach; breakfast is a buffet with both Thai and Western dishes, and the à la carte lunch and dinner menus draw a lot of praise for being tasty and quick, the softshell-crab spaghetti in particular coming up again and again.

To be straight about it, the Wi-Fi here is weak and in some rooms barely connects · If you need to work online or be connected all the time, that can frustrate — but if you see Koh Mak as a chance to unplug, it actually plays into the experience · A couple of guests also note that some staff have limited English, and breakfast gets crowded and slow at peak times, though the team stays courteous · The hilltop rooms also involve a bit of walking up and down the slope, so if that's a problem, choose a beachfront villa instead.

On location and getting there, you have to understand the nature of Koh Mak first — it's a small island with no big roads or convenience stores like you'd find in town · From the resort you can cycle or take a short ride to the island's other restaurants and bars · Getting here from Bangkok means a road trip to Laem Ngop pier in Trat, then a speedboat across to Koh Mak, with the resort helping arrange the pier transfer · A score of 9.0 from around 66 Trip.com reviews is high and steady — a sign most guests leave happy.

The honest summary: Mira Montra is one of the best resorts on Koh Mak for anyone who wants quiet, a private beach and attentive service at a reachable price · Lovely villas, a sea-view pool, good food, free kayaks and SUP · The things to accept are the weak Wi-Fi, the uphill walk to the hilltop rooms, and the crowded breakfast at peak times · If you can live with those three and you're coming to Koh Mak to genuinely rest, this place delivers real value.

A tip from following the reviews here for a while: if you want to be right on the sand and skip the hill, book a Beachfront Villa — don't grab the cheapest rate and end up on the hilltop without realising · Come to Koh Mak with the mindset of unplugging; don't expect strong Wi-Fi · Use the free kayaks/SUP in the morning when the water is calm for the most fun · In high season (November–April) Koh Mak gets busy, so book ahead and lock in a free-cancellation rate · In the rainy season many island resorts close, so check boat schedules and opening dates before you plan.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Mira Montra Resort Koh Mak

faq.q: Where is Mira Montra Resort Koh Mak and how do you get there?
faq.a: The resort sits on Ao Phra Beach on the north side of Koh Mak, Trat Province · Getting here from Bangkok means a road trip to Laem Ngop pier, then a speedboat across to Koh Mak, with the resort helping arrange the pier transfer · There are no big convenience stores on Koh Mak; you can cycle or take a short ride to the island's other restaurants.

faq.q: How much does Mira Montra Koh Mak cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. ฿2,500/night for the Hilltop Sea View Room · they rise to the Deluxe Villa and Beachfront Deluxe Villa (one-bedroom villas), up to the two-bedroom Family Villa · Prices vary by season and package, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is the Wi-Fi at Mira Montra any good?
faq.a: The Wi-Fi here and across Koh Mak is fairly weak, barely connecting in some rooms · If you need to be online constantly, bring a backup mobile data plan · But if you see Koh Mak as a place to unplug and switch off, this actually plays into the experience.

faq.q: Who is Mira Montra Koh Mak best for?
faq.a: It's best for couples, honeymooners and families who want a quiet resort, a private beach and attentive service at a reachable price · It suits people who came to rest and switch off and who enjoy gentle water activities like kayaking and SUP · It's not the place for nightlife or anyone needing strong internet.

faq.q: Which room should I pick — how do the hilltop rooms differ from the villas?
faq.a: If you want to be by the sand without an uphill walk, choose a Beachfront Villa · The Hilltop Sea View Room is the cheapest option, set on the hill with a bit of climbing but a lovely sea view · Villas add the bonus of bathtubs, outdoor showers and more privacy.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book and when's the best time to go?
faq.a: The best time for Koh Mak is high season (November–April), with clear seas and good weather — book 3–6 weeks ahead as this is a popular island resort · In the rainy season (May–October) the island goes quiet, some resorts and shops close and boats run less often, so check opening dates and boat schedules before booking · Pick a free-cancellation rate if your plans aren't firm.
